requirements.text: Change the background into a basketball court
requirements.source_phrase: Change the background into a basketball court

outcomes.description: Change the image background into a basketball court.

nodes.question: Is the edited background as a whole recognizably a basketball-court setting, rather than merely containing basketball-related objects or a court-like floor?
nodes.criteria: pass: the background as a whole is recognizably a basketball-court setting, with contextual court features beyond isolated basketball props or a limited strip of marked floor. fail: the background is clearly not recognizable as a court setting, even if basketball objects or limited court markings are present. unknown: the background is not sufficiently visible or clear to decide.
nodes.binding: Assess the edited background as a whole for a recognizable basketball-court setting. A hoop, balls, or limited floor markings alone do not establish completion when the surrounding backdrop remains plain or otherwise not court-like.

nodes.question: Is there visible evidence that the background has been changed toward a basketball court, even if it is not recognizably a complete court?
nodes.criteria: pass: visible background elements or alterations specifically indicate progress toward a basketball court, though the result may be incomplete. fail: no such progress is visible, or visible evidence shows no basketball-court-directed change. unknown: the background evidence is insufficient to determine whether such progress occurred.
nodes.binding: Visible changes to the background that specifically indicate an attempt to make it a basketball court.

nodes.question: Does the image show the background changed into a basketball court?
nodes.criteria: Use only the saved statuses and image-grounded evidence from n1 and n2. complete: n1 passes—the background as a whole is recognizably a basketball-court setting. partial: n1 fails and n2 passes—specific basketball-court-directed background progress is visible, but the setting is not recognizably complete. absent: n1 fails and n2 fails—no requested change has progressed. unknown: either support is unknown, or the evidence does not establish which of complete, partial, or absent applies. A known negative observation is evidence, not uncertainty; unrelated edits do not count as progress.
nodes.binding: Compose all support observations to assess the requested background change: distinguish a recognizable court setting as a whole from specific but incomplete basketball-court progress. Do not treat props or limited markings alone as proof of completion.

program.checker_template:
Execute the supplied check and return status, image-grounded or dependency-grounded evidence, reported confidence from 0 to 1 (or null), and used_dependency_ids.
For a support node, inspect SOURCE and EDITED only for its ONE saved visual proposition. Return pass/fail/unknown according to the criteria; fail is usable negative evidence, not automatic uncertainty. Never assess overall fulfillment or predict an expected label. used_dependency_ids must be [] because the evidence checks are independent.
For a requested node, NO IMAGES are supplied. Use ALL and ONLY the saved dependency observations for visual evidence, together with the original instruction, rubric, binding and saved composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Explain how the dependency observations support the selected state, naming their IDs. used_dependency_ids must list every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in the saved order. Do not invent visual observations, silently replace dependency findings, or count supporting facts as completed edits. If necessary evidence is missing or contradictory, return unknown. Confidence is self-report, not a calibrated probability.
